idea.name: CareerHound job board
idea.one_liner: A paid job board for US job seekers that scrapes openings from company websites and charges for access.
idea.customer: People in the US who are employed or unemployed and looking for a job.
idea.offer: A job-search board that collects jobs directly from company websites, behind a hard paywall.

acquisition_channels.details: Researches niche content on Instagram, Reddit, and TikTok, then uses repeatable video and text formats. Paid creators produce content that directs viewers to CareerHound.
Uses creator marketplaces to find creators; Roman says most are found by DMing people who already make content.
DMs are used to recruit paid content creators, not to acquire job-seeker customers.

ideas.delivery: The site scrapes job listings from company websites and presents them to job seekers behind a subscription paywall. Roman coordinates creators using a sheet of content formats and instructions; the founder does not need to be the on-camera personality.

tools: social-view tool transcribed as 'used to order mice' (name unclear)

ideas.other_uk_rules: If operated in the UK, check UK GDPR duties for any personal data in scraped listings or user accounts, subscription disclosures and cancellation requirements under the DMCC Act, and whether the service's activities bring it within the Employment Agencies Regulations 2003. The transcript's DMs recruit creators rather than acquire job-seeker customers; assess PECR if reproducing that outreach in the UK.
